issues.description: The solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents with a boolean parameter (getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests)), but the problem statement and UML specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters. This parameter mismatch is structural: students will be instructed to implement a no-argument method while the solution uses a different signature, which can confuse learners and break automated tests or comparisons.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the specification by changing the solution method signature to public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() (no parameters). Implement it to return the total number of students (inscribed + guest) as required by the task and update any internal calls (e.g., getNameAndTotalNumberOfStudents and getNumberOfStudentsPerTutor) to use the no-argument method. If conditional behavior (include/exclude guests) is needed, provide a separate overloaded or private helper method, but keep the public signature matching the UML and problem description.

issues.description: The problem statement and template specify a no-argument method getTotalNumberOfStudents(): int, but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This changes the API/identifier usage for the same conceptual operation (obtaining the total number of students) and forces a different call convention. Students following the problem/template will look for a no-arg getTotalNumberOfStudents method and may be confused when the solution requires a boolean parameter to include guest students.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the problem/template by providing a no-argument method public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns the total (including guests if that is the intended default). If conditional inclusion of guests is desired, consider adding an overloaded method public int getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) while keeping the no-arg signature to preserve the originally specified API.
